analysis.title: Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the US Midterms
key_insights: Morgan Stanley calls the market reaction to the US midterms an overreaction and recommends a selective 'Buy the Drop' strategy. It prefers hyperscalers, select semis, infrastructure and time-to-power names that have de-rated, and software enablers and AI adopters.

The firm expects the election to push out projects, not cancel them. About 5GW of US projects not yet under construction in Texas and Ohio move from 2028 to 2029. That is 20% of US projects and 10% of global projects. 2027 projects under construction are unchanged.

US data center additions are now down 4% y/y in 2028 (19.9GW vs 24.9GW before) and up 38% y/y in 2029 (27.6GW vs 22.7GW before). Globally, additions are up 9% in 2028 and 20% in 2029. US cumulative capacity for 2028 is cut to 105GW from 110GW. Global capacity for 2028 is cut to 219GW from 224GW.

Hyperscaler capex forecasts are unchanged in aggregate at $1.6T for 2027 and $1.8T for 2028. There is a possible downward bias to 2028 if builds are delayed. Per-company forecasts for GOOGL, META and AMZN are also unchanged.

The 2028 US power shortfall widens to 44GW (38% of demanded power) from 38GW (33%) after the delay. The bottleneck is shifting from compute to the powered shell stage. Near-term grid-connected power gains scarcity value.

The delay could create an air-pocket in the 2028 tech supply chain. Reduced component undersupply, weaker pricing power, inventory builds and a traditional down-cycle of slowing orders and margin normalization are possible even if AI demand is intact. Valuations already price much of this in, and the key risk is margin sustainability.

Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa's platform includes a moratorium on new data center approvals, and Ohio's Governor-elect Acton proposed a conditional one. Both apply to new approvals, not projects already permitted or under construction. Durable measures need legislatures. The Texas House is Democratic and the Senate Republican, and the Ohio Senate keeps a Republican supermajority. Georgia is more incremental.

Democrats won both the House and Senate and flipped governorships in Ohio, Texas and Georgia. The firm does not expect a federal pause, citing the national-security framing and a likely veto. The binding levers sit with state commissions, legislatures and county boards.

Compute efficiency gains become more important, and Meta is targeting a 10X compute efficiency improvement in 2027. This favors the largest, best-capitalized players that can invest in first-party models. Hyperscalers can also shift builds to friendlier states like Tennessee and Louisiana.

In semis, compute (NVDA, AVGO) and memory (MU, SNDK) are preferred over analog and networking. NVDA is the top pick. NVDA and AVGO trade at about 9x CY28 P/E. The risk is that a slower GW build lets supply catch up with demand and hurts pricing for the most in-shortage components, especially memory and Intel.

Morgan Stanley's strategists say the Philadelphia semiconductor index is down about 40% since mid-June and the correction is nearer its end. A final retest is possible on positioning and technicals. They expect price action to resolve upward into 2027 and recommend adding de-rated quality cyclicals.

Data center capex is about 5% of 2027 S&P 500 consensus revenue, and mid-single-digit in 2028. The strategists say the S&P is priced at 18x forward earnings, near Liberation Day valuation levels, and nears its 7100 to 7300 support range.

ASML is the best-positioned European semi and a Top Pick. The firm says the price implies 93 low-NA EUV tools in FY28 and 16.6x FY28 consensus EPS, below prior trough multiples. It keeps a EUR 1,700 target on 25x FY28 EPS of EUR 68.47.

Powered shell providers diverge by exposure. WULF, RIOT, HUT and APLD are less exposed to Texas dynamics, while CIFR, GLXY and MARA carry more risk of delay or moratorium. The firm assigns a 75% probability that CIFR's Colchis and GLXY's Helios II and Merlin I receive approvals. RIOT's Corsicana lease shows 33% yield on cost.

Power equipment and IPPs have contractual protection. BE, SEI, VST, TLN and CEG are high-conviction Overweights even if data center growth is slower. GEV and INIO are more sensitive to oversupply but have valuation support. The firm prefers PJM-exposed IPPs (TLN, CEG) over ERCOT and is negative on utility SO.

Credit: AI-related debt issuance is $543bn year to date versus $216bn for FY25. Hyperscalers are about 60% of supply. The firm expects higher AI issuance in 2027, greater scrutiny for new construction financing and neoclouds, and it prefers colocation over hyperscaler data center ABS. About $80bn of data center construction debt was issued this year.

ORCL has three roughly 1GW campuses (Jupiter in NM, Lighthouse in WI, Shackelford in TX) in states with incoming governors signaling restrictions. They carry over $50bn of construction loans. MS credit stays cautious on ORCL and does not yet recommend stepping in.

Asia and other regions could absorb about 20GW of US spillover (27GW in the bull case). Asia power winners are Gulf Development, Keppel, Adani Power, Yangtze Power, Samsung SDI and Hokkaido Electric. KEPCO, Tata Power, Global Power Synergy, Huaneng and EPDC are to avoid.

The firm sees alpha shifting from AI semis and infrastructure to software and AI adopters. 44% of S&P 500 companies cite a quantifiable AI benefit, up from 32%. Preferred software includes MSFT, SNOW, DDOG, MDB, DT, NET, PANW, CRWD and OKTA. Forward EPS is rising faster for adopters that discuss quantified benefits.

China AI could benefit from a US slowdown, and the firm favors CXMT and Cambricon for China GPU demand. Europe strategists say the AI enabler rotation is overdone. LatAm has copper price risk (Chile, Mexico) and IT hardware export risk for Mexico (US-bound exports up 101% y/y in 9M26).

Within multi-industry and machinery, new data center entrants (ACCV, FPS, CARR) are at most risk, while legacy leaders (VRT, ETN, TT, JCI) should prove more durable. Rental companies (URI, WSC, TH) look oversold, and CAT, CMI and EROC are most exposed to continued de-rating.

sector_views.sector: Data center ABS and colocation credit
sector_views.rationale: Stabilized assets benefit from slower competing development, and colocation is preferred over hyperscaler ABS.

earnings_insights: ASML (MS estimates): the firm models 94 EUV shipments in FY27 and 111 in FY28. Management capacity commentary of 90 tools in FY27 and over 110 in FY28 fell short of investor expectations. FY28 EPS estimate is EUR 68.47 vs Visible Alpha consensus EUR 77.93.
ASML: at EUR 1,250 and a 20x two-year forward P/E, the market implies FY28 EPS of EUR 62.5, 20% below Street. MS says it implies 93 low-NA EUV tools in FY28, 16% below consensus.

Microsoft (guidance): management guided to 49-50% cc Azure growth in 2Q and said its outlook already includes some third-party GPU capacity shifting into 2HFY27. MS retains FY27/FY28/FY29 capex estimates of about $238bn/$298bn/$358bn.

Oracle (company targets, per MS): about 3GW of capacity as of FY26 (May 2026), about 850MW delivered in the latest quarter, and a target of 10GW by FY28. About $220bn of capex is needed with net investment about 50% lower via vendor financing and prepayments.
INNIO (3Q26 reported, per MS): 19GW of contracts at end of 3Q26, of which MS estimates about 12GW are firm orders.
GE Vernova (FY3Q26, per MS): 122GW of gas under contract. MS sees 30%+ EBITDA growth beyond 2028 and about $14bn of base-case 2028 EBITDA.
Riot Platforms (3Q26 earnings note): the Corsicana deal generated a 33% yield on cost. Rent is projected to begin in September 2027 on 910MW of critical IT load.
CoreWeave: Helios site in West Texas has Phase I (133MW) delivered in July and Phase II (260MW) starting 2Q27. Management said moratoriums affect where infrastructure is built, not demand.
Hyperscaler 3Q26 results confirmed AI growth, but stocks did not react positively and not all companies met high expectations, per MS Asia semis.
Sandisk (MS estimate at $835 share price): buybacks near 50% of revenue could retire more than 50% of the company by end of 2028.

Williams: management targets commercializing 1-2 behind-the-meter projects by year-end with 3-4 hyperscalers in late-stage talks. MS forecasts about 16% 2025-30 EBITDA CAGR vs the company's 11%+ outlook.
Liberty Energy: signed a 1.2GW development agreement with an AI lab, targeting the first roughly 500MW energy service agreement by December 2026. MS says power could exceed 50% of EBITDA.
PROPWR (ProPetro): about 510MW of contracted capacity expected by early 2028 and a 2.6GW target by YE2032. MS forecasts power above 70% of consolidated EBITDA.

risk_factors: Labor requirements tougher than expected, bans on on-site fossil generation (as in Virginia), or stricter emissions limits could cut data center deployments below MS projections.
A 2028 air-pocket across the tech supply chain could reduce pricing power or build inventory, with margin sustainability the key risk.
Delays beyond 2028 would lower demand for on-site power and large gas turbines, and power equipment could be viewed as past peak.
Financing headwinds from investor angst, and greater scrutiny of new construction financing and neoclouds, may matter more than slower construction.
Texas PUCT appointments by the incoming governor and 765kV transmission treatment are wildcards for utilities.
ORCL single-site execution at Jupiter, Lighthouse and Shackelford, with over $50bn of short-dated construction loans, could pressure sentiment.
Mexico IT hardware exports, Chilean copper and other US-linked supply chains are exposed if US data center energization slows.
Semis earnings may need to come down in coming years if the AI build-out is slower, and tech may not outperform until relative earnings momentum improves.
Persistent permitting, labor and materials constraints could bias 2028 capex downward and prolong the cycle.

vol_and_positioning: MS composite sentiment and positioning indicator is nearing capitulatory levels but is not yet at March selloff levels.
A final retest of lows is possible on positioning and technicals, notably leveraged ETF and macro systematic supply flagged by MS QDS, and on whether correlation spikes.
Investor sentiment in semis has become substantially more bearish, and valuations already reflect concern about earnings durability.
The median MS semis stock is down 53% from its 52-week high and the average is down 48%.
Further de-grossing of the AI trade could add pressure on midstream stocks.
DLR and EQIX shares show higher beta to AI-related headline volatility, which creates short-term price risk.
geopolitical: US midterm results: Democrats won both the House and Senate and governorships in Ohio, Texas and Georgia, with state-level data center restrictions the main AI-relevant channel.
Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa proposes a moratorium on new data center approvals, and Ohio Governor-elect Acton proposes a conditional moratorium and requirements on new projects.
Texas Gov. Abbott ordered an audit of ERCOT data center projects in August and ERCOT delayed its Batch Zero study. ERCOT certification meetings are scheduled for December 10 and 17.
No federal pause is expected given the national-security framing and likelihood of a presidential veto.
Bipartisan US-China technology and national security rivalry persists, so MS expects selective rotation within China equities rather than a broad geopolitical re-rating.
Potential Iran de-escalation could add pressure on midstream stocks and lower oil and yields, which would help Chinese airlines and chemicals.
Recent Middle East regional conflict may have reduced the near-term attractiveness of the region as a host for US data center capacity.
Virginia's ban on on-site fossil fuel generation is cited as a risk model for other states.
Pennsylvania's governor announced stricter guardrails on data center development, which affects Nebius's GW-scale site.

tension_points.theme: data center build delay vs derailment
tension_points.bull_case: MS sees a push-out of about 5GW from 2028 to 2029 rather than a cut. Hyperscaler capex is unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T, and a longer cycle improves credit and lease rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Delays on top of labor and materials constraints could put downward bias on 2028 capex. Prolonged restrictions could cut total build-out over five years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tougher labor requirements, bans on on-site fossil generation like Virginia's, or tougher emissions limits that lower deployments. MS also tracks Texas bills and the December 10 audit finalization.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is intact and undersupplied at the compute level, valuations already price in a peak, and a longer cycle lifts multiples.
tension_points.bear_case: With 2028 growth near flat, the supply chain could see slowing orders, margin normalization and earnings downgrades, especially in memory and components.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Order cancellations or delays from power equipment and hardware suppliers, or industry demand moving into outright contraction.

tension_points.bull_case: MS strategists say price action resolves upward into 2027 as sentiment nears capitulation and valuations are low.
tension_points.bear_case: A final retest is possible on leveraged ETF and macro systematic supply, and tech cannot outperform until relative earnings momentum improves.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The S&P 500 breaking below the 7100 to 7300 support range or a final spike in correlation.
